title: Sales/CS batch normalization and quick-scope for enterprise asks
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description: Create a repeatable, minimally prescriptive pipeline to normalize batches of enterprise feature asks from Sales and Customer Success, produce a 1-page quick-scope for each consolidated ask, and hand off to engineering/design for feasibility and estimate. Goal: cut initial scoping latency from ~10 business days to <= 48 hours for obvious high-value asks and to provide consistent inputs for prioritization and commercial negotiation.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical intake template that converts raw CS/Sales requests into a normalized feature request payload (fields: problem statement, affected accounts, revenue signal, frequency, compliance constraints, business priority, suggested SLA)
A lightweight scoring rubric (impact, effort, revenue risk, customer tier) that auto-generates a priority band (A/B/C)
A Quick-Scope one-pager generator that produces a 1-page mini-PRD for each consolidated batch with expected owner, rough FTE/point estimate band, and required stakeholders
Integration points defined with Eng and Design for a 5-business-day feasibility window or an expedited 48-hour fast track for top-tier accounts
Hand-off checklist and Slack/GDrive template links included in the playbook
Pilot run completed with three Sales/CS account cohorts and feedback logged
notes: 2026-03-01: Kickoff with Sales (Marisol) and CS (Daniel) — collected 17 raw asks across three named accounts (FinServ-A, Retail-B, Health-C). Agreed to test batch-normalization on weekly cadence.

2026-03-03: Drafted normalization schema (fields + enumerations). Shared with ENG for feasibility on automated scoring. ENG requested clarified descriptions for 'revenue signal' and 'frequency' fields.
2026-03-04: Design reviewed quick-scope layout. DES suggested moving acceptance criteria up and adding a compliance bullets section for regulated accounts.
2026-03-05: PM triage session produced priority bands for initial 17 asks: 5 A-band, 8 B-band, 4 C-band. Marked 2 items for expedited legal review (data residency).

2026-03-07: Internal sync with ENG-Infra to confirm engineering can commit a 48-hour fast-track feasibility slot for up to 2 items/week when account ARR > $250k. ENG asked for a tech checklist to accompany the one-pager.
2026-03-08: Prepared pilot plan and invited stakeholders. Blocker: need Sales to provide signed NDA for Health-C before we can share detailed compliance artifacts.
decision_log: Use a simple numeric scoring (0-10) across four axes: Impact (customer business gain), Effort (estimated eng/ops work), Revenue exposure (monetary or churn risk), Compliance complexity. Weighted sum => priority band.
Quick-scope will be limited to one page and must include: Problem, Who it helps, Business outcome, Minimal success criteria, Rough effort band, Dependencies, Compliance notes.
Pilot will run for 3 weeks with weekly batch runs and a retro at the end to tune scoring weights.
If a request requires cross-org security approval, mark as Blocked until appropriate documents are available; do not slow other scopes in the batch.
tasks: Implement auto-scoring prototype in spreadsheet (PM + Data Analyst)
Design quick-scope template and GDrive generator (Design)
Create engineering feasibility checklist and fast-track process (Eng)
Run pilot with three account cohorts and capture feedback (PM + Sales + CS)
Document hand-off tooling and Slack workflow (PM + EngOps)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sales provides incomplete context causing rework — Mitigation: mandatory minimum fields and a 1-hour live intake slot per batch
Risk: Legal / compliance delays — Mitigation: flag and parallelize initial technical feasibility that does not require PII access
Risk: Engineering capacity for fast-track — Mitigation: cap to 2 fast-track items/week; schedule during low-deploy windows
pilot_plan: Week 1: Normalize and score 17 historic asks; generate quick-scopes for top 8; collect ENG quick-feasibility responses
Week 2: Run live intake with Sales/CS on 5 new accounts; measure time-to-scope and stakeholder satisfaction
Week 3: Retro and weight-tuning; finalize playbook and launch internal doc
communication_plan: Weekly cadence: Friday 30-min sync with Sales, CS, Eng, Design during pilot
Channel: #pm-enterprise-intake for real-time notifications and hand-offs
Deliverable: End-of-pilot summary slide deck and recommended next steps
